header:
Date: 2027-03-21
Time: 15:00 - 16:03 UTC
Duration: 63 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Anita Singh (Solaris Head of ML Eng), Tom Bates (Platform Lead), Lara Ng (Security), Priya Menon (Product)
summary: POC scoping focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling: Solaris wants to validate latency/cost and run benchmarks on a subset of production traffic. Key success criteria discussed: latency SLOs, throughput, cost per 1M tokens, and parity on accuracy for 3 representative flows. Action items: share proposal, security docs, dataset; run 10k-sample benchmark; schedule infra deep-dive.
transcript: [00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro - i'm maya, account exec on redwood, with diego our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?

[00:14] Anita Singh: Hi Maya, thanks. we're good. we've been looking at inference platforms, want to scope a POC to validate latency/cost and see if we can move some chat and doc automation to redwood's runtime.

[00:28] Diego Ramos: Great. high level today we'll map your traffic, agree success criteria, and propose a small benchmark plan that we can run on your sample set. we'll also cover security needs for private deployments if needed.

[00:42] Tom Bates: Quick note - our infra is mainly on AWS EKS, some GCP for analytics. we expect to run the POC initially in your hosted env, but we need clear options for VPC/private later. latency tail is important for our SLAs.
[01:00] Maya Chen: Totally. can you walk through the three main product flows you mentioned in the email? that helps define traffic shapes and token distributions.

[01:12] Priya Menon: Sure - Flow A is customer support chat: short prompts, avg input ~30 tokens, output ~90 tokens, really latency-sensitive (p95 < 500ms ideally). Flow B is account summarization: users request month-end summaries, input ~120 tokens, output ~300 tokens, throughput lower but longer outputs. Flow C is compliance/regulatory parsing: batch jobs, inputs vary widely up to 2k tokens, outputs also large - latency less strict but accuracy critical.
[01:50] Diego Ramos: Helpful. do you have QPS numbers per flow or concurrency peaks?

[01:56] Anita Singh: For prod, Flow A peaks 40 requests/s during business hours, sustained avg 12 qps. concurrency between 25-60. Flow B averages 2 qps, spikes to 8. Flow C is batch nightly, about 80 concurrent jobs but run as async batch windows.
[02:18] Maya Chen: Good signals. for the POC what are you hoping to prove?

[02:22] Anita Singh: Three things - one, can you meet latency SLO for Flow A at our target QPS; two, does the model quality match our baseline (we'll provide eval set); three, what's the projected cost per 1M tokens under realistic batching/kv-cache.

[02:39] Diego Ramos: We typically scope a POC with a benchmark harness: we'll run your 10k sample queries representing the three flows against a couple of candidate model variants and runtime configs. we'll capture p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput, GPU utilization, and cost estimates. we also track accuracy metrics you provide.

[03:05] Tom Bates: Important: we need to see network egress patterns and ensure request routing doesn't violate our data residency. also encryption at rest and KMS integration for any private deployments.
[03:18] Lara Ng: yes SOC 2, SAML SSO are musts. for POC hosted we'll need contractual protection and clarity on logs retention - we don't want customer data persisted beyond the benchmark window.

[03:34] Maya Chen: Understood. we have SOC 2 and ISO docs; i'll share them. for hosted POC we can enable short retention and disable persistent logs - we'll note that in the proposal. we support SAML/SSO and KMS integrations for private runs.
[03:50] Priya Menon: On the model side, are you recommending an open model or your vetted catalog?

[03:55] Diego Ramos: For banking use-cases we usually start with a few open models we've profiled - smaller quantized variants for latency-sensitive chat, and larger ones for summarization/accuracy. redwood also has pre-baked quantization profiles and recommended batching configs. we can test 2-3 variants in the POC.
[04:12] Anita Singh: Can you give a rough estimate of how many concurrent requests a single dedicated GPU node can handle for our flow A?

[04:20] Diego Ramos: ballpark: with a 4090-style or A10G node and a 7B-ish quantized model, with batching and prefix caching you might sustain 200-400 rps under optimal batching, but tail latency and small-batch arrival patterns reduce that. for real-world guidance we model effective concurrency: for average input ~30 tokens and output 90 tokens, we expect 8-20 parallel in-flight requests to meet p95 targets under hosted optimized runtime. it's really sensitive to sequence length distributions and request burstiness.
[05:02] Tom Bates: When you say '200-400 rps' that seems high - can you clarify the difference between raw token throughput and request-level concurrency?

[05:09] Diego Ramos: absolutely - 200-400 rps is token-generation-limited when batching long sequences; for short chat requests the per-request overhead and latency SLOs typically cap effective rps. we will run a traffic model that maps avg input/output tokens, desired p95 latency, and batching to estimate required GPU capacity.
[05:32] Priya Menon: what's the expected cost delta between hosted vs dedicated for a POC of this size?

[05:38] Maya Chen: hosted POC pricing is usage-based and easier to spin up - it's slightly higher per-token but no infra commit. dedicated/reserved gives better unit economics at scale; for the POC we usually recommend hosted to iterate quickly, then move to a small dedicated pool for more realistic capacity testing.
[05:55] Anita Singh: timelinewise we want results in two weeks if possible - is that realistic?

[06:00] Diego Ramos: yes - if you can provide the sample set and query distribution within 2-3 business days we can provision the harness and run the 10k-sample benchmark within 5 business days, then we analyze and present results. so 10 business days total is feasible.
[06:18] Lara Ng: on security we need details: where logs are stored, who can access them, key rotation, and whether you support HSM-backed keys for private deployments.

[06:28] Maya Chen: we support customer-managed KMS for private deployment, HSMs via partner integrations, and detailed audit logs for Dedicated/Private. hosted POC can have tightened retention and role-based access enabled; we'll include specifics in the security pack.
[06:42] Tom Bates: for the benchmark harness - can you simulate our real traffic burstiness? we have some extreme bursts during incident flows.

[06:50] Diego Ramos: yes we model burstiness. part of the deliverable is a traffic model: QPS baseline, peak QPS, concurrency, and token distribution (P50/P90/P99 for both input and output). we'll run both steady-state and burst tests to capture tail behavior.

[07:06] Anita Singh: let's talk numbers - current production metrics: avg total requests across all flows ~15 qps, peak 48 qps, overall concurrency around 70. token distribution: median input 45, p90 input 180, median output 100, p95 output 650 (some long summaries), 99th occasionally near 1500 tokens.

[07:34] Diego Ramos: that's extremely helpful. with those numbers our traffic model will recommend either a small dedicated pool for stable performance or a hosted config with autoscale and burst buffering. we'll show costs for both.
[07:46] Priya Menon: accuracy - we'll provide an eval set for Flow B and C. what metrics do you typically report?

[07:52] Diego Ramos: we capture exact-match, ROUGE for summarization, and a custom relevance metric per your labels. we produce a quality report mapping model outputs to your baseline, plus regression alerts if quality drops compared to baseline.

[08:10] Maya Chen: no worries. we'll also include suggestions: quantization profile, KV cache enablement for repetitive prompts, and batching knobs. those often reduce cost 20-60% depending on workload.
[08:22] Tom Bates: network egress - for hosted POC where data passes through your public endpoints, will the data ever land unencrypted on third-party storage?
[08:30] Maya Chen: no. we encrypt in transit and at rest. for hosted POC we can set short retention and no persistent indexing. we'll provide the flow diagram in the security pack.
[08:42] Lara Ng: and SSO - we need SAML integration and SCIM provisioning for any consoles used during the POC.
[08:48] Maya Chen: supported - we'll share our SSO integration guide.
[08:52] Anita Singh: about the benchmark outputs - can you include per-token cost extrapolations for 1M, 10M tokens under different batching profiles?

[08:59] Diego Ramos: yes, that's standard. we'll run the benchmark with realistic batching, then run cost models: naive (no batching), moderate batching, and optimal batching with KV cache. we also show an operational forecast for monthly spend given your projected traffic.
[09:18] Priya Menon: are there any specific observability hooks we can use? tracing, per-token breakdowns?

[09:23] Diego Ramos: Redwood Console exposes per-route latency, token cost breakdown, and tracing hooks. for POC we can enable an extended retention demo so you can inspect traces and token-level cost for the sample runs.
[09:36] Tom Bates: Ok, next - acceptance criteria. we want p95 latency < 600ms for Flow A at 40 qps sustained and no more than 10% drop in accuracy vs baseline for Flow B and C. does that align?

[09:49] Maya Chen: sounds reasonable. we'll formalize success criteria in the proposal: p50/p95/p99, cost per token caps, and quality regression thresholds. if we don't meet the criteria we iterate configs (quantization, batching) and re-run.
[10:02] Anita Singh: what about private deployment timeline? we might want a VPC/private instance after the POC - how long to stand that up?

[10:09] Diego Ramos: for Private with your VPC and customer-managed KMS, typical lead time is 4-8 weeks depending on network reviews and any on-prem requirements. we'll start with hosted POC to validate before booking the private deployment slot.
[10:23] Priya Menon: please call out any blockers - e.g. if the POC requires synthetic traffic tooling or additional infra access.

[10:29] Maya Chen: blockers: access to representative query set and QPS traces, an internal stakeholder for acceptance testing, and signoff on data handling for the benchmark. we'll include a checklist in the POC doc.
[10:40] Anita Singh: sounds good. can you send the pricing sheet and proposed SLA for the POC?

[10:45] Maya Chen: yes i'll send a POC proposal with pricing options (hosted vs small dedicated), security docs, and the benchmark plan by EOD Friday. diego will run the initial profile after we get the sample set.

[10:58] Diego Ramos: final note on traffic modeling: we'll produce a small CSV model mapping request-size buckets to required GPU-seconds and expected cost; that helps you budget and decide dedicated pool size.
[11:10] Tom Bates: perfect. last thing - do you have references of similar banks or regulated customers who've done a POC?
[11:17] Maya Chen: yes, we can share redacted case studies; i'll attach a quick reference list in the follow-up.
[11:24] Priya Menon: thanks everyone, excited to get the dataset to you. let's aim to reconvene next tuesday after results are in.

[11:30] Maya Chen: thanks all. recap: we will send POC proposal, security docs, request dataset and QPS traces, plan to run 10k-sample benchmark and return results within ~10 business days. any other items?
[11:43] Anita Singh: no, that's it from us. thanks.
[11:46] Maya Chen: thanks, meeting closed.
[11:50] -- End of Recording
